q: What does the Ghazipur brick cluster use in energy each season?
title: Ghazipur brick kilns: a season's coal
short: About 302,600 t of coal, 181,632 toe, across some 380 kilns fired in 2017-18. A typical Ghazipur kiln burns 788 t for 44 lakh bricks, 18 t per lakh, at 1.51 MJ per kg of fired brick: a quarter to a third more than a well run fixed chimney kiln needs.
audience: Brick kiln owners in Ghazipur district

ul: About 480 brick units; about 380 kilns fired in 2017-18.
Almost all fixed chimney Bull's trench kilns making handmade solid clay bricks; a few use zigzag firing.
A typical kiln fires about 25,000 bricks a day, January to June.
Coal is almost all of the energy.

p: A well run fixed chimney kiln needs 1.1 to 1.2 MJ per kg of fired brick, a zigzag kiln 0.9 to 1.1. At 1.51, a Ghazipur kiln reaching 1.2 would burn about a fifth less coal, about 162 t a season.

ol: Coal by invoice and weighbridge slip, with the GCV the supplier states.
Bricks fired, by class, and days fired.
Any firewood or crop residue, on its own line.

p: Brick kiln rules notified in 2022 push fixed chimney kilns towards zigzag or other approved firing, so a conversion is often due anyway. The ledger above is the before figure that shows what it saved.

example.title: One kiln, one season (estimate)
lines: 788 t coal for 44 lakh bricks: 179 kg per 1,000
At India's coal factor: 788 t x 1.76 = 1,387 t CO2, 315 kg per 1,000 bricks
The profile implies coal near 6,000 kcal per kg; at about 2.26 t CO2 per tonne: 1,781 t, 405 kg per 1,000
Reaching 1.2 MJ per kg: 162 t less coal, 285 to 366 t CO2 a season
Cluster: 302,592 t coal, at least 532,600 t CO2
example.note: Coal, output and energy from TERI's Ghazipur brick cluster profile (2017-18). The higher factor applies the IPCC bituminous default to the implied heat value; your coal's GCV decides.
